evidence.quote:
Figure 1
(A) POCUS-TTE performed pre-thrombolysis, showing a markedly dilated right ventricular cavity. Parasternal long-axis view showing acute dilatation of the right ventricle and pulmonary annulus, resulting in incomplete coaptation of the pulmonary valve cusps secondary to an abrupt increase in pulmonary artery pressure (white arrow). (B) POCUS-TTE performed pre-thrombolysis, showing sudden right ventricular pressure overload. Parasternal short-axis view showing the main pulmonary artery trunk with functional pulmonary regurgitation (white arrow).

Performed at 14:00, the POCUS-TTE examination confirmed the physiological impact of acute RV strain (Figure 1A,B), demonstrating severe RV dilation (46 mm below the tricuspid annulus), markedly reduced systolic function (tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion, TAPSE = 12 mm), and paradoxical interventricular septal motion resulting in a “D-shaped” left ventricle (LV)—findings consistent with acute RV pressure overload [RV-right atrium (RA) pressure gradient 40 mmHg].

assignments.rationale: Caption names pre-thrombolysis POCUS-TTE of the index case and the case narrative cites Figure 1A,B for the same examination; no identity inferred from pixels.

panels.detailed_description: A wide, low-resolution grayscale CT image labelled "MIP 3.5mm" at upper left, "R" at the left edge and "L" at the right edge, and a short label at the top center that reads approximately "SP". The vertebral body and spinal canal appear at the top center with ribs curving on both sides, so the image is displayed with the posterior chest at the top and the heart at the bottom. Both lungs are dark. Contrast-enhanced central pulmonary arteries are bright, and in the mid-chest there is a bright contrast-filled chamber at the lower left of the heart region. Two white arrows point at the hilar regions: one from the lower left toward a gray, lower-attenuation filling defect beside bright contrast in a vessel on the image-left (R) hilum, and one from the upper right toward a similar gray defect next to bright contrast in a vessel on the image-right (L) hilum. A round gray structure lies beside the vertebra on the image right. A few fine branching bright vessels radiate into each lung.

POCUS—TTE post-thrombolysis. Complete resolution of intracardiac thrombus following Emergency Department thrombolysis.
